newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippines says to shop for rice from neighbours.
newsitem.headline: Philippines says to shop for rice from neighbours.

text.p: The Philippine's National Food Authority (NFA) will shop for more rice from its Asian neighbours to beef up the country's buffer stocks before July this year, NFA assistant administrator Vic Racho told Reuters on Thursday.

Racho said the NFA would shortly review an offer from Vietnam after the NFA got approval from President Fidel Ramos to import up to 650,000 tonnes of the staple before the third quarter, which is the lean period for Philippine rice output.
Traders from Pakistan, India and China have also offered to supply the rice requirement of the Philippines, he said.
"We are looking for suppliers from our neigbours now," Racho said.

The NFA has so far contracted 55,000 tonnes of Thai rice for delivery in March and April. "Under the same agreement, we have an option to buy an additional 150,000 tonnes of rice from Thailand," Racho said.
Early this month, a source in the Thai Rice Exporters Association told Reuters in Bangkok the Thai rice sold to Manila was priced at $300 per tonne.
Manila traders said Vietnam has offered to sell rice to the Philippines at a cheaper price, or $5 to $10 lower than the $300 per tonne price of the Thai rice.
The Philippines has imported 1.2 million tonnes of rice from Thailand, Vietnam, India and the United States between July 1995 and June 1996 to meet the shortfall in domestic production, Racho said.
Racho said Philippine rice stocks was at 1.8 million tonnes at the start of February this year, of which around 300,000 tonnes are in NFA warehouses.
The Philippines consumes an average of 22,000 tonnes of rice per day, Racho said.

An official from the Philippine Agriculture Department said last month he expected the country's buffer rice stocks to fall below the ideal 90-day level, or around 860,000 tonnes, before July this year.
The government has set 1.98 million tonnes, or stocks sufficient for three months, as the ideal rice buffer to be maintained to avert a shortage.
An acute shortage in 1995 had made the government extremely unpopular as rice is the staple of the country's 68 million people. -- Manila newsroom (632) 841-89-36, fax 817-62-67
